targets.title: Audience costs, information, and credible commitment problems
targets.evidence_quote: As I mentioned above I replicate Moon and Souva (2016), who examine the effect of audience costs on the probability of failed threats using the Militarized Compellent Threats (MCT) data (Sechser, 2011).
targets.outcome_computational_quote: In Model 1, the replication is done without adding any growth rate variable, but excluding the observations that are dropped when the annual growth rate variables are used because of the availability of GDP data (only from 1952 onwards).
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: This is to show that the reduced number of observations does not cause the category of high audience cost capacity and no strategic territory to lose its presumed effect on the probability of successful coercive diplomacy. As expected, this category is associated with a lower probability of failed threats.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original analysis is re-estimated on a restricted original sample rather than rerun to recover the original numbers. The author explicitly says the original association survives the sample restriction. Added economic interactions test novel predictions and their failure does not refute Moon and Souva’s original finding. Robustness confidence is limited because later models leave the original coefficient nonsignificant but do not discuss this as a challenge to the original.
